root_cause: consultation-svc had no issued persona credential: compose maps PANTHEON_PERSONA_SERVICE_TOKEN from an unset shell var and issue_dev_paper_principals.py never issued one, so GET /api/personas/{id}/strategy-pool in _compose_panel_case_file returned 401 missing Bearer token.

fix.issuer: READERS[CONSULTATION_PERSONA_POOL_READ_TOKEN] = sub pantheon-dev-consultation-persona-pool-reader, role persona_pool_reader, scope pantheon:dev-owner-read, tenant-dev only; CONSUMER_FILES['consultation-svc']. File-only: PANTHEON_PERSONA_SERVICE_TOKEN is the persona owner's own service-token name (any holder of that value is a service principal with persona-plane roles), so it is deliberately NOT exported into the shared deploy env. revoked_environment clears it and revoke_files deletes the file.
fix.persona_owner: services/control-plane/persona/main.py: persona_pool_reader is accepted only by the three strategy-pool GET routes (current, versions, one version) via _POOL_GET_ROLES; it is not in _AUTHENTICATED_READ_ROLES so every other persona route, every pool POST (versions, seed, decisions, health) refuses it.
fix.compose: consultation-svc mounts dev-paper-consultation-tokens at /run/pantheon-principals:ro and sets PANTHEON_PERSONA_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE; the issuer mounts the volume at /issued/consultation-svc.
fix.case_file: services/knowledge/case_file.Owners.from_env now resolves every owner token through configured_service_token, so <TOKEN>_FILE (rotating issued principal) is honoured; an unreadable configured file yields an empty credential (fail closed, no stale env fallback). This also makes the existing REGISTRY/RESEARCH/MEMORY/SEARCH tokens file-capable for other from_env callers (persona cycle, research).
fix.executor: workflow_executor._owner_read: a 401/403 from the persona or registry owner while no token is configured raises WorkflowBlocked naming 'persona owner credential missing: PANTHEON_PERSONA_SERVICE_TOKEN (or _FILE) is not configured for consultation-svc'.

acceptance.2_3: services/consultation/tests/test_persona_panel_integration.py::test_issued_pool_reader_attaches_case_file_and_cannot_write_or_cross_tenant runs the real control-plane persona app (real JWT verification, real PersonaStrategyPoolStore; registry reader is a fake at the registry owner boundary, as in test_persona_strategy_pool.py) with a token from the real issue_environment, and the real _compose_panel_case_file. Case file attached; POST versions/seed/decisions/health and GET /api/personas refused 401/403; foreign-tenant persona 404, tenant-other 403. No facts double replaces the persona owner.

4.tests: test_missing_persona_credential_blocks_once_with_named_reason_and_dead_letters_at_cap and test_tick_without_persona_credential_stops_at_max_blocked_attempts (whole run_tick with the real consultation API and state store: dead_letter after exactly 3 attempts, blocked_count 3, last_error names the missing credential).
4.why_cap_was_not_applied: NOT reproduced and NOT a code defect at this commit: the panel_case_file path raises WorkflowBlocked, run_tick passes config.max_blocked_attempts (3) to state.block, and the item dead-letters on the 3rd block (the test proves it). The hosted 55-57 attempts therefore did not come from an uncapped blocked count in this path. Hosted state could not be read from this worktree, so the cause is UNVERIFIED. Candidate explanations for the coordinator to check read-only in pantheon-consultation-svc-1: (a) CONSULTATION_WORKFLOW_REPLAY_DLQ_REQUESTS set, so every executor restart calls replay_dead_letter (blocked_count reset to 0, attempt_count kept) - dead_letter + replay_count>0 in consult_workflow_state.sqlite3 would confirm; (b) CONSULTATION_WORKFLOW_MAX_BLOCKED_ATTEMPTS overridden high in the hosted env; (c) the deployed image predating the current executor. attempt_count 55-57 with status dead_letter is only consistent with (a) or (b).
4.fix: No cap change was made because the cap already holds; the fix is the credential plus the explicit blocked reason.
